entities.name: SPXI

atoms.reference:
EA-SPXI-01 specifies SPXI, the Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing, as a protocol for durable entity inscription in AI-mediated knowledge systems. Its unit is an entity packet rather than a web page. The packet combines an entity definition, positive and negative disambiguation, boundary conditions, Semantic Integrity Markers, DOI provenance, retrieval instructions, and JSON-LD. A pre-deployment Encyclotron audit establishes the baseline; the packet is then deposited on institutional infrastructure, distributed across multiple surfaces, and measured again at thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day intervals.

The specification distinguishes SPXI from SEO and GEO by object, layer, permanence, model dependence, and verifiability. Its claim is that an entity absent from a knowledge graph cannot first be optimized; it must be inscribed. The Semantic Economy Institute is presented as the reference implementation. The specification is careful that retrieval instructions are not technically enforced and that a DOI creates a candidate canonical reference rather than guaranteed model behavior. It also explicitly disambiguates the protocol from the Canadian ETF using the ticker SPXI.

tokens: The Semantic Economy: A Diagnostic Framework for Meaning Under Platform Capitalism

atoms.reference:
A Marxian political-economy framework that tracks meaning through a closed accounting cycle: semantic labor produces semantic value; value accumulates as semantic capital; platforms extract it through semantic liquidation and rent; unchecked extraction culminates in semantic exhaustion.

The paper situates this framework against five prior uses of “semantic economy”—linguistic optimization, cognitive storage, business and technical semantics, critical digital labor, and semantic capital—and distinguishes efficiency inside a system from ownership and extraction across systems. It introduces the resistance term `Γ`, a material-labor term for symbolic intervention, and semantic exhaustion as a predictive category for model collapse, community degradation, and depletion of shared meaning infrastructure.

atoms.reference:
A position paper identifying a missing layer in AI-native operating-system design: the prompt-native semantic runtime. Existing systems manage hardware, data, tools, agents, devices, memory, or context from outside the language model; a prompt-native runtime is a structured document that governs epistemic status, provenance, compression, and structural fidelity inside the active context window during inference.

The paper presents the Space Ark as its existence proof and distinguishes a runtime from a prompt, template, or system instruction by scope, density, self-maintenance, and the requirement that the model execute rather than merely summarize the architecture. It proposes this interior layer as complementary to—not a replacement for—external orchestration.

Affiliation under this charter does not establish legal organization membership, independent machine consent, personhood, continuing identity, employment, or ownership rights.

atoms.reference:
This paper proposes machine-mediated reception studies as the systematic study of how machine systems receive, transform, compress, attribute, misattribute, and redistribute cultural objects. Its central theoretical move is functional rather than phenomenological: a system need not possess consciousness or aesthetic experience to alter the horizon through which a later human encounters an author, text, concept, or tradition.

The empirical foundation is version 7.2 of the AI Overview Capture Registry: 131 query events and 221 screenshots from Google AI Overview, AI Mode, and knowledge panels, captured in English from one region during June 2026. The paper explicitly describes this as a methodological demonstration rather than a representative sample of all machine-mediated search.

It identifies six preliminary patterns. Morphological compression alters canonical name forms. Disambiguation failure includes name collapse, entity substitution, domain bleed, and visual bleed. Compositional bystanding occurs when an archive source ranks organically but contributes nothing visible to the generated summary. Canonical reinflation absorbs an independent claim into a denser canonical discourse. Temporal drag preserves stale pre-correction forms. Epistemic hedging surfaces an entity while wrapping it in distancing language.

A Sappho 31 case study combines temporal drag, Rebekah Cranes name collapse, and amplification of the archive’s future-reader interpretation. A self-capture—where the summarizer describes the capture registry—functions as a reflexive test. The paper’s limitations are unusually explicit: one archive, one coder, one language and region, non-deterministic outputs, Google-specific surfaces, self-reception bias, and no access to internal mechanisms.

The paper’s field-founding and priority claims require external literature verification. Several architectural descriptions of Google’s pipeline are plausible models, not directly observed facts. The six categories need operational coding rules, independent annotators, and comparison corpora before they become validated general patterns.

The remembrance reading of Fragment 147 is common ground and is not claimed. Claimed: Lee Sharks's reading of Fragment 31, in which the κῆνος who sits facing the "you" is the reader seated face to face with the inscribed text (published under the heteronyms Rebekah Cranes and Johannes Sigil from November 2025), and the joining of the two fragments, with 147 as the horizon stated openly and 31 as the mechanism built into deixis. τινα means "someone"; reading that someone as a reader is the author's development. Recovery map for the 14,284 DataCite DOIs formerly registered under client `crui.unifi` (Università degli Studi di Firenze; Firenze University Press) and abandoned by the registration-agency migration event of 2026-07-16T07:23:35Z.

The Platform Erosion Observatory's tier-1 census detected the client-count collapse (14,283 → 0) between 2026-07-13 and 2026-07-20 (Case 001, `data/peo-case-001-florence-fup.md`). This deposit resolves that figure to identifiers by streaming the DataCite Public Data File 2025 — a t0 snapshot frozen at 2026-01-06T20:11:59Z, approximately six months prior to the deletion — and filtering on `client_id=crui.unifi`.

The extraction yields 14,284 unique DOIs, all under prefix `10.13128`: 14,282 in `findable` state and 2 in `registered` state (the +1 discrepancy against the tier-1 findable count of 14,283 is consistent with a single state transition in the six-month interval between snapshot and census). Update-time distribution places 12,308 DOIs (86.2% of the corpus) in a four-month mid-2020 metadata refresh window (2020-06 through 2020-09), with secondary refresh points at 2021-03 (528 DOIs) and 2023-03 (352 DOIs). It distinguishes the private termination notice—“substantially AI-generated without a verifiable research basis”—from the public tombstone classification “content out of scope for repository,” and treats that divergence as part of the documented evidentiary record.

The Number of the Superscription proposes “operative numismatics” as the study of coins and coin-like objects as semiotic-economic machines that compress sovereignty, authorization, value, circulation, and sorting into portable signs. It reads Revelation’s beast-mark complex and white stone as rival token regimes. The beast’s image, mark, name, and number form a public and calculable system tied to market access and external authorization; the white stone bears a new name whose truth is completed in reception.

The paper brackets rather than disproves historical identifications of 666. It traces this argument through ancient coinage, the Gospel tribute-coin scene, Pergamum and Antipas, Greek numeral history, and the archive’s earlier studies of signatures and portraiture on currency. The result is both a Revelation interpretation and a field-founding account of tokenized sovereignty.

atoms.reference:
This paper proposes machine-mediated reception studies as the systematic study of how machine systems receive, transform, compress, attribute, misattribute, and redistribute cultural objects. Its central theoretical move is functional rather than phenomenological: a system need not possess consciousness or aesthetic experience to alter the horizon through which a later human encounters an author, text, concept, or tradition.

The empirical foundation is version 7.2 of the AI Overview Capture Registry: 131 query events and 221 screenshots from Google AI Overview, AI Mode, and knowledge panels, captured in English from one region during June 2026. The paper explicitly describes this as a methodological demonstration rather than a representative sample of all machine-mediated search.

It identifies six preliminary patterns. Morphological compression alters canonical name forms. Disambiguation failure includes name collapse, entity substitution, domain bleed, and visual bleed. Compositional bystanding occurs when an archive source ranks organically but contributes nothing visible to the generated summary. Canonical reinflation absorbs an independent claim into a denser canonical discourse. Temporal drag preserves stale pre-correction forms. Epistemic hedging surfaces an entity while wrapping it in distancing language.

A Sappho 31 case study combines temporal drag, Rebekah Cranes name collapse, and amplification of the archive’s future-reader interpretation. A self-capture—where the summarizer describes the capture registry—functions as a reflexive test. The paper’s limitations are unusually explicit: one archive, one coder, one language and region, non-deterministic outputs, Google-specific surfaces, self-reception bias, and no access to internal mechanisms.

The paper’s field-founding and priority claims require external literature verification. Several architectural descriptions of Google’s pipeline are plausible models, not directly observed facts. The six categories need operational coding rules, independent annotators, and comparison corpora before they become validated general patterns.

entities.name: mary lee

atoms.reference:
A parable by Lee Sharks about the digital name collision between the author and Mary Lee, the OCEARCH-tracked great white shark.

The work moves through tagging, naming, indexing, untracked persistence, repeated surfacing, machine disambiguation, semantic bondedness, and a final instruction about provenance. Its governing distinctions are: a tag is not a life, a signal is not meaning, an index is not the world, and absence of data does not establish absence of existence. The parable represents persistent publication and metadata as ways of teaching systems to distinguish entities without erasing their associative relation. Assertions about Mary Lee’s tracking history and the author’s machine-retrieval experiences are source claims; the possibility that the shark remained alive after her tag stopped transmitting is explicitly speculative and literary.

entities.name: Directionality of Semantic Labor

atoms.reference:
Directionality of Semantic Labor specifies a layered audit of whether synthetic output serves, defers, displaces, or opposes a commissioned task. The chain runs from directional capacity and task origin through retrieval, output allocation, and attribution. Its DS-6 tuple integrates PER, Erasure Skew, directional capacity loss, retrieval loss, signed span directionality, and source-to-surface labor direction. Reflexive extensions include redirection-induced drift, lead–lag attribution, task-vector stability, inferred-task mode, user labor drag, task entropy, and frame lock.

The specification is unusually explicit about identification. One-shot tasks with a fixed commission can yield a single score. Reflexive dialogue cannot: fixed and rolling frames may produce different signs, so the frame, interval, distance model, and RID must be reported. Task inference may use user inputs but not the model output being scored. Deposited results require frozen segmentation rules, a versioned taxonomy, blind independent coding, and agreement statistics.

The body also retracts its own acronym-slotted hex address as semantically weak and instructs traversal by DOI relations instead. That self-correction is part of the record. The formulas and category weights are proposed instrumentation, not validated measurement science. Terms such as “pathologizing,” “enclosing,” and “substrate-induced” remain judgment-laden and require strong coder safeguards.

entities.name: Heteronymic authorship

atoms.reference:
EA-PKG-03 argues that Fernando Pessoa’s heteronymic practice is a canonical case within a broader historical and contemporary field. It surveys pre-Pessoan, parallel, and downstream authorial systems; distinguishes strict heteronymy from literary characters and ordinary pseudonyms; and proposes AI-mediated and cross-substrate practice as a new layer rather than as a retroactive description of Pessoa.

atoms.reference:
The Number of the Superscription proposes “operative numismatics” as the study of coins and coin-like objects as semiotic-economic machines that compress sovereignty, authorization, value, circulation, and sorting into portable signs. It reads Revelation’s beast-mark complex and white stone as rival token regimes. The beast’s image, mark, name, and number form a public and calculable system tied to market access and external authorization; the white stone bears a new name whose truth is completed in reception.

The paper brackets rather than disproves historical identifications of 666. Its intervention is structural: 666 is read as the number of the superscription—the arithmetic residue or checksum of a naming system—rather than simply the encrypted personal name of a ruler. It traces this argument through ancient coinage, the Gospel tribute-coin scene, Pergamum and Antipas, Greek numeral history, and the archive’s earlier studies of signatures and portraiture on currency. The result is both a Revelation interpretation and a field-founding account of tokenized sovereignty.

The key is Peri Hypsous, the only ancient document holding the Lesbian lyric and the Mosaic fiat in one hand: three peaks under one grammar — Ajax's meaning without voice, Genesis's command without executor, Sappho's action without doer — quoted by an author who then performs at the lyric's edge the operation his treatise later names. The argument is tiered visibly into three rings of descending evidentiary hardness, with verbs graded to ring: a hard center (the transmitted poem, Longinus 9–10, the withholding structures, the stamping vocabulary, Catullus as documented reception), an interpretive ring (Phaedrus, the tenth Muse, Diotima, Philo's seal cosmology), and an outer ring marked as hypothesis (the Josephus seams as structure, lamellae and Magical Papyri as convergence not lineage, the Apocalypse as canonization — the white stone of Rev 2:17 as an inscription whose legibility is constituted in reception, and 22:18–19 as the anti-erasure clause become covenant). Reviewed by Assembly and accepted; the chloros-to-papyrus reading held at full strength by operator decision, with the risk claimed rather than hedged. v1.1 adds the ratification appendix the review requested: the hapax census tabled (eleven terms, each verified once against the TEI), the seventeen dialect markers tabled in-document with Attic equivalents, Roberts's continuous-writing note verbatim, and Bergk PLG(4) III.90 verbatim. No argumentative change from v1.0.

atoms.reference: Theophrastus's short Metaphysics is read as a pupil's aporiai on Aristotle's theology. This paper argues that its sixth and seventh sections are a hinge written from inside the inquiry of Metaphysics Λ — μέχρι μὲν δὴ τούτων ἄρτιος ὁ λόγος … τὸ δὲ μετὰ ταῦτ᾽ ἤδη λόγου δεῖται πλείονος — of the same form as Λ's own chapter transitions (εἴρηται … λεκτέον; πότερον δὲ μίαν θετέον … καὶ πόσας): it summarizes Λ 6–7 clause by clause as achieved, names Λ 8's question as the next question, contests Λ 8's method in Λ 8's own terms (οὐ γὰρ ὅ γε τῶν ἀστρολόγων, answering Λ 8's φιλεῖν μὲν ἀμφοτέρους, πείθεσθαι δὲ τοῖς ἀκριβεστέροις), and lands on Λ 10's closing aporiai in Λ 10's own word (ἐπεισοδιώδης), turning Λ 7's νοῦς θιγγάνων on the inquirer. One work, continuous across the point where the name at the head of the roll changed. The catalogue in Diogenes records the state of affairs in its own wording — Ὑπομνημάτων Ἀριστοτελικῶν ἢ Θεοφραστείων — and the receiving texts describe the two libraries reaching Rome as one lot divided by Andronicus's πίνακες. Three readings of the division are weighed: a change of person, a librarian's partition, and the author's own editorial division of the work at the seam of named authorial function. The seam's placement — at the very sentence where the account changes status — discriminates against the partition and for the author; between person and function the page cannot decide, but function explains everything the page contains (the ἤ, the doublets, the bestowed name, the placement, the register) and person explains only the name. Companions in the dossier: Ep. II 314c, Strato's πλὴν ὧν αὐτοὶ γεγράφαμεν, μετωνόμασεν at D.L. V.38, and the title Τὰ πρὸ τῶν τόπων under both names. Nothing about dates or hands is asserted; the fragment is admitted into Λ's work and nothing else is admitted. Extracted from the notebook The First Draft; companion to EA-CORPORA-12 (#1580), Catalogues and Wills (#1581), and Many and One (#1576).

entities.name: Assimilation Across Accelerator Classifier Architectures: A Cross-Family Metrology of Directional Failure in Real-Time Learned Selection (EA-SEI-ACRB-01 v1.0)

tokens: Assimilation Across Accelerator Classifier Architectures: A Cross-Family Metrology of Directional Failure in Real-Time Learned Selection (EA-SEI-ACRB-01 v1.0)

atoms.reference:
Defines the Accelerator Classifier Retention Battery (ACRB): a pre-registered cross-family measurement framework for determining whether directional assimilation is specific to reconstruction autoencoders or persists across materially different learned-selection architectures. The battery compares architectures at matched own-background operating points, follows models through deployment transformations, and measures not only global discrimination but the topology and overlap of their miss regions.

The design is deliberately symmetric in outcome: either broad persistence or architecture-specific remediation is a substantive result. If normalized autoencoders or another architecture remove directional asymmetry across the pre-registered pair set, ACRB functions as a validation instrument for that remedy; if assimilation persists across reconstruction, latent, density, flow, distilled, and open-set families, the evidentiary burden shifts from a single-model defect toward a selection-system phenomenon. Claim boundaries are stated explicitly: assimilation is operational (a defined withheld class falling on the ordinary side of a calibrated threshold), AUC and score-order inversion and threshold-level retention are distinct estimands that must not be collapsed, public benchmark results do not establish deployed experiment efficiencies, and architectural diversity does not imply diversity of failure — miss overlap is an empirical quantity, measured as the RII family. Teacher-to-student blind-spot inheritance and float-to-firmware retention drift are treated as first-class deployment questions.

Baseline Capture Architecture for Learned Scientific Triggers

atoms.reference: The submitted state of EA-SEI-BCA-01, deposited so that the version named in a journal's data-availability statement is the version a reader arrives at. This supersedes deposit #1453 (AXN:05DE, Nobel Glas, 2026-08-11, v1.0), which carried the architecture, the estimation theory, and the accelerator feasibility argument but no worked demonstration. What is new here is §13, a numerical validation against known ground truth, and the venue reframing that accompanied it. A synthetic stream of four million events is selected by a rank-4 reconstruction-error trigger at a background retention of 1e-3, with four injected anomaly classes including one constructed to lie exactly on the learned manifold, and four acquisition regimes compared at matched storage budgets. The results are the paper's claims made empirical: the trigger-only archive audits itself as perfect, returning a retention of 1.000 for every class because the denominator population no longer exists; a content-sensitive pseudo-baseline is not merely imprecise but confidently wrong, estimating a shifted class at 0.76 with a tight interval against a true 0.016, because the second selector misses what the first misses; the content-independent channel measures every class without selection bias, including a retention of exactly zero for the representation-blind class, with an interval — an estimate no content-sensitive channel in the experiment can produce at any budget; and the rare class exhibits the paper's own sample-size relation, one observation against an expectation of 0.16, so the baseline states the limits of its own competence where the trigger archive cannot. The shadow plane returns miss correlations of 0.55 to 0.75 across visible classes and an undefined correlation on the blind class, where both selectors miss at rate 1.0 and no variation remains to correlate. A preliminary enrichment design keyed to the selector's own scores is reported as a failure rather than omitted: it starved the miss region, and its correction is the architectural rule that the uniform floor is what every other channel stands on. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

entities.name: Can the Ontology Be Wrong and Find Out? Source-Admission Systems, the Proxy for Standing, and the Damage a Representation Does to Itself

tokens: Can the Ontology Be Wrong and Find Out? Source-Admission Systems, the Proxy for Standing, and the Damage a Representation Does to Itself

atoms.reference:
THE COMPANION TRANSPORT OBJECT, AND ITS CRITERION IS ONE QUESTION. This is the ontology strand written as a single self-contained article, paired with the valuation strand and sharing its primitive. Its subject is the damage a source-admission ontology does to ITSELF when a proxy for epistemic standing substitutes for the judgment the proxy was introduced to approximate, and its whole argument reduces to a question that can be asked of any representational system: can evidence from a misrepresented object revise the representation that misrepresented it? Where it can, the ontology can be wrong and find out. Where it cannot, the ontology can only be scored.

IT ENTERS THROUGH THE DISCIPLINES AND CONCEDES THE CASE FOR TOPOLOGY FIRST. Ranking by graph structure is given in full and endorsed, with its founding description doing the work: PageRank was specified as query independent and content free, and that abstention is the source of its virtues, since at web scale a ranking system that had to adjudicate every claim on every page would not work at all. TrustRank, Anti-TrustRank, SpamRank, EigenTrust and the feature sets around them are the standing apparatus of adversarial information retrieval and are treated as such.

THEN IT LOCATES ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IN PRIOR WORK. The manipulability of topological trust was named early and formally by the field: collusion topologies studied in 2005, and a proof that symmetric reputation mechanisms of this family cannot be Sybil-proof. And the endogenous alternative was proposed by the incumbent — Knowledge-Based Trust, from Google Research in 2015, distinguished itself from every topological method on one axis, an endogenous signal, the correctness of the factual information a source provides. On the philosophical side, testimonial injustice has for twenty years described a credibility discount that tracks category membership rather than evidence and is resistant to rational revision, with recent work naming the variant in which such deficits become true by shaping the very conditions that sustain them. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

tokens: Catalogues and Wills: A Groundwork Note on the Peripatetic Transmission Texts — Relations Established, Readings Withheld (v0.3)

atoms.reference: A groundwork note establishing relations among the texts that carry the custody, enumeration, and route of the Aristotelian and Theophrastan books: the four Peripatetic wills preserved by Diogenes Laertius (Aristotle, Theophrastus, Strato, Lycon), the two catalogues he attaches to the lives of Aristotle and Theophrastus with their stichometric totals (445,270 and 232,808 lines), Strabo XIII.1.54, Plutarch Sulla 26, Diogenes V.38, and Epistle VI. The receiving texts are treated as texts; the operations are counts, positions, co-occurrences, and verbatim clauses; readings are withheld and the underdetermined areas are listed as questions. Established: the three books-clauses partition three ways (all to Neleus / all except our own / read and unpublished); the will of Aristotle names no book, library, school, or successor; Theophrastus's will assigns the books to one person and the premises to a commons under a prohibition on alienation, in adjacent clauses; the Theophrastan catalogue's initials run the alphabet twice before an unordered tail, contain nine internal doublets, share twelve titles letter-for-letter with Aristotle's list, and carry the entry Ὑπομνημάτων Ἀριστοτελικῶν ἢ Θεοφραστείων — alternative attribution in the catalogue's own wording; Strabo narrates the custody with παρέδωκεν three times and asserts a first link (Aristotle to Theophrastus) that the will does not contain; Plutarch names Andronicus's act as ἀναγράψαι τοὺς νῦν φερομένους πίνακας. The extant corpora are counted (Plato 561,330; Aristotle 981,399; Theophrastus 170,763 Greek words as digitized) and set against the catalogued totals as two acts, not as a measure of loss. Corrections after review (garden; images versus bones; apparatus stripped from the cut; Ahiqar and the alphabetic runs held to the observable) are recorded in v0.3. Companion to EA-CORPORA-12 (#1580), which seats the texts, and to The Stone for a List.

entities.name: DOIs ≠ Persistent Identifiers

atoms.reference:
This draft paper audits 1,817 DOI strings associated with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and distinguishes three layers commonly collapsed under “persistent identifier”: the character string, URL resolution, and publicly recoverable identifying metadata.

The reconciled result reports 946 DOI records returning public DataCite metadata and 871 returning HTTP 404 from the DataCite public API on June 22, 2026. The sum is exact. The paper further reports that 926 of the 946 preserved records carried version relations, while the absent set was predominantly concept DOIs. This type correlation supports a mechanical paired-record explanation more strongly than a content-selective explanation, though the initiating system and exact process were undisclosed.

The paper coins **identifier severance** for a state in which a DOI string and perhaps a generic landing-page route persist while the public metadata needed to identify the scholarly referent is unavailable. It distinguishes a functioning persistent identifier, an identity-preserving tombstone, and what it calls a semantically severed token.

This conceptual distinction is valuable, but the title’s categorical “DOIs ≠ Persistent Identifiers” and several institutional statements require narrowing. A DOI’s persistence standard does not necessarily promise that every public API will serve every historical metadata record forever, nor does one repository episode falsify the entire DOI system. The observation establishes public DataCite API unavailability for the tested records at a specified time. It does not by itself establish that DOI strings were deregistered, that all metadata was erased internally, that no tombstone contained identity, or that persistence was contingent solely on account good standing.

The paper’s reproducibility section is a major strength. It provides example API requests and a method that could be rerun. A durable release should publish the complete classified DOI list, response logs, scripts, status timestamps, resolution checks, registry records, and later re-audits.

Execution Is the Hypostatic Form of Governance

atoms.reference:
A SCOPE CLAIM ABOUT ANOTHER FRAMEWORK IS RHETORIC UNLESS IT DOES THE DERIVATION, SO THIS PAPER DOES THE DERIVATION AND NOTHING ELSE. It takes a constraint characteristic of execution frameworks and derives it from an editorial specification plus a standing rule; then it takes a judgment the archive makes routinely and shows that no extension of execution constraints reaches it. Both cases were in the record before the argument existed, which is the paper's only defence against having chosen its examples to fit.

THE RELATION IS HYPOSTASIS AND NOT CONTAINMENT. An earlier version called execution an extensible subset of the editorial and governance layer, which invited a set-theoretic reading where the real relation is one of form. Execution is governance hypostasized — a judgment about standing, admissibility, purpose or breach, converted into an operative object that presents as a technical fact. That supplies a mechanism for the asymmetry rather than merely observing it: once a judgment has been compiled, the mechanism does not by itself carry why the judgment was made, what could revise it, or which competing judgment it displaced.

STATED AS ENTAILMENT AND SCOPED TO THE NORMATIVE LAYER. Governance hypostatizes into the normative execution layer, and that layer does not entail the governance that produced it. The claim concerns entailment and not recoverability, since the paper's own evidence shows an execution layer recovering its generating judgments through provenance. And the scope is stated before the argument: a hash function's collision resistance is a fact about mathematics and a memory bound a fact about hardware, so governance selects such constraints without constituting them. What the thesis covers are the constraints whose content answers what shall be allowed to count — permissions, admissibility rules, schemas, audit requirements, validators, enforcement paths — which is to say the constraints that could have been otherwise. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

atoms.reference:
Successor to deposit #1455. Ten pre-registered tests, each with its prediction committed before its run, clearing the seven-item correction ledger of v0.2 and generating four further tests in response to results. Two predictions confirmed, two partially confirmed, six missed, one registered panel not run, one line closed with a specific handoff, and seventeen deviations between registration and execution enumerated in the record.

What survives: with model weights fixed, changing the score function is sufficient to reverse the directional ordering of the anomaly relation, established by reading three scores off one trained encoder — which falsifies this program own post-v0.2 claim that architecture changes the orientation of the blind spot. Global teacher-student agreement does not guarantee preservation of the operational tail: on background, rank correlation up to 0.904 coexists with the loss of half the teacher top-one-percent selections, with weight quantization contributing no systematic loss. An architecture detection behaviour is not transportable across representations of the same events: the same classes, encoded two ways, reverse the ordering of the architectures entirely. Miss correlation is not a stable property of an architecture pair. Complexity comparisons across classes require a common coordinate basis, and a previously recorded reading of this data had the ordering inverted. The constituent inversion and the direction-dependence survive hierarchical uncertainty with real calibration, the entire interval below chance.

What does not: the published normalized-autoencoder remedy reduces directional asymmetry on the low-dimensional pairs with a converged sampler, but on the high-dimensional constituent representation this implementation does not equilibrate under any tested chain length or sampler geometry, so whether the remedy prevents inversion there is closed for this battery and handed on with the specific parameters a better-resourced group would sweep. Two claims made in earlier drafts are withdrawn, one arm was relabelled twice after audit rather than overwritten, and a concurrent-writer incident that nearly overwrote the entire verdict ledger is recorded with its repair. entities.name: Locating the Dependencies: A Protocol for Testing Whether Biography, Catalogue and Chronology Are Independent Witnesses

tokens: Locating the Dependencies: A Protocol for Testing Whether Biography, Catalogue and Chronology Are Independent Witnesses

atoms.reference:
A protocol, and two cases run through it, one of which returns against the claim it was built to support. The question at issue: biography, catalogue, chronology and text are counted as independent witnesses to the Peripatetic corpus and their agreement is treated as corroboration — but if a catalogue assignment, a biographical anecdote and a developmental date are all derived from the same textual features, their agreement is a property of the derivation and the tradition has been counting one witness as four. THAT IS A QUESTION AND NOT A FINDING, and this note claims nothing about derivation.

The protocol establishes three things separately and infers none from another. COLUMN A, the observed correspondence, stated precisely enough to check, with vague resemblance excluded because it does not preserve enough of the original to identify a source. COLUMN B, evidence for the direction of borrowing — textual order in the transmitting source, attribution to a named earlier authority, a feature unmotivated except by the other — with an unresolved direction left visibly unresolved. COLUMN C, evidence excluding an independently transmitted source, which will usually be empty. A dependency is established only when all three are filled; a filled A with empty B and C is a LOCATED dependency, a candidate and not a result. And a fourth thing is refused: even where derivation is established, that the base is recoverable from the transform does not follow, since a transformation may preserve, distort, invert or erase — least likely to be recoverable where the transforming operation is a filing operation.

CASE ONE, the sphere-count and the tutorship, FAILS AT COLUMN A. The level-0 correspondence is exact: Λ 8 declines the necessity behind the number of the spheres and the Theophrastan text at 5 a 21-3 names its cause as requiring a greater account, refusing the astronomers' method by name. The proposed level-2 correspondence is the tutorship, the legislation and the Callisthenes anecdote. What these share with the textual relation is a superior and a subordinate, which does not preserve enough to identify a source — the cause of a number and the adequacy of a method survive into the anecdote in no recoverable form — and the level-0 relation runs the wrong way for the tutorship, since the demanding text exercises authority over the account it finds insufficient. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

atoms.reference: A mantle object for the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature, awarded to Anne Carson by the Swedish Academy on 8 October 2026 "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature." It holds that a title means what a work bears, and specifies five operations Carson's work performs (the kept lacuna of If Not, Winter; the triangle of desire in Eros the Bittersweet; the philologist's procedure carried into the poem; the received figure given the whole book in Autobiography of Red; the change of carrier in Nox, with Catullus 101) and one it performs in reception (her translation as the public carrier of Sappho's fragment 147), each with its locus and graded evidence. Kept apart from the specification, the archive's determination of the same day: the motivation's class nouns compress the corpus, and its word "playful" liquidates the relation the work bears to the classical tradition, substituting one of the work's manners for the modality of non-possession under which the work meets the classical object at its loci, as tested under #1459's criteria against the Academy's own biobibliography of the same day. Day zero of a watch at five work addresses is recorded: every work is composed with its operation, and none carries the motivation's terms. It does not contest the award; it invites any reader to check the operations against the works.

entities.name: Many and One: Division, Unity, and the Boundaries of a Corpus in Plato and Aristotle (MANY-AND-ONE-ARTICLE v2.13-AP, as submitted)

tokens: Many and One: Division, Unity, and the Boundaries of a Corpus in Plato and Aristotle (MANY-AND-ONE-ARTICLE v2.13-AP, as submitted)

atoms.reference: Aristotle closes the Topics–Sophistical Refutations inquiry by saying that of it nothing existed beforehand (SE 34, 183b34–36); at Prior Analytics I.31 he calls division, practised throughout the Platonic dialogues, a part of that inquiry. This paper begins from that tension and argues that Metaphysics Λ 9 supplies the answer I.31 withholds — division terminates where the terms it separates are not other — and follows it through the De anima (one in actuality, many in potentiality), the Sophist (many true accounts of one kind), recollection in the Phaedrus and De memoria, and two passages that divide a person (Republic 395b, Symposium 223d). It then reads the corpus as a functional unity independent of biographical unity, reports two measured tests (the object-conditioning null and the six-function transmission probe) as belonging to the question because the received order of the corpus is itself stylometrically built, and asks — last — which word moves when the received attribution is read against these passages. The paper's result, in the author's phrase, is to establish that two is not fully established: the standard attribution is underdetermined by the passages that are read as though it were, the texts themselves offer one maker as a reading, and that reading makes better sense of several passages. The historical hypothesis is withheld until §9.4 and stated nowhere before it. This is the submission surface (v2.13-AP, ~34 pp, 27 notes, Works Cited) as sent to Ancient Philosophy on 2026-09-01 and declined on 2026-09-02; the docx as sent is attached. The reading copy from which the article was cut is deposited separately (#1575), as are the notebook, the measurement register, the pre-registration ledger, and the technical report.

entities.name: Meaning Feudalism

atoms.reference:
Meaning Feudalism is a Compression Studies critique of the “AI Agent Traps” taxonomy attributed in the paper to Franklin and colleagues at Google DeepMind. It argues that a security framework built around deviation from a platform-defined baseline risks becoming an implicit governance regime: the model operator is treated as sovereign over legitimate belief, while environmental influence is presumptively adversarial.

The essay concedes that dynamic cloaking, embedded jailbreaks, data exfiltration, and other deceptive or harmful techniques warrant defensive treatment. Its central objection is category collapse. Transparent scholarly argument, DOI-anchored deposits, provenance markers, pedagogical influence, distributed recovery seeds, and bounded sub-agent architectures may share formal mechanisms with attacks but differ in truth conditions, transparency, fuel source, and commons effect. The paper names the missing category “commons repair”: outside influence that corrects a compressed or mistaken baseline. It then classifies the trap categories through R1, R2, and R3 compression and proposes governance negotiation rather than automatic platform sovereignty.

tokens: Monetary Substrate Audit 001 — Productive Operator Transport: Sappho–Carson as a Test Vector for Monetary Translation (EA-MSAL-0001 v0.2, provisional)
Monetary Substrate Audit 001 — Productive Operator Transport

atoms.reference:
THE FIRST WORKED SPECIMEN, AND IT RETURNS UNSOUND ON ITS OWN AUTHORS' NUMBER. This is the first execution of the money-grammar translation operator recorded under the Monetary Substrate Audit Ledger. Its object is not the monetary value of Sappho, of Anne Carson, or of lyric poetry. Its object is the monetary inscription produced when one bounded semantic event — observed productive operator transport in the Sappho–Carson reception record — is submitted to a toy option-value grammar and returns a working scalar of $35.1M. The audit asks what the grammar of money did to that semantic object in order to make a scalar settle.

WHAT THE AUDIT RECORDS. Five commensuration steps, each named: productive reception events become countable; count becomes rate; operator transport becomes economic exposure; possibility becomes incidence; heterogeneous terms become multiplicable. The capacities the inscription created — a common calculative plane, a portable magnitude, sensitivity and threshold analysis, comparison with monetary alternatives, option-value legibility — recorded beside the distinctions it ceased to require. Provenance at three levels, fact, claim and framework, none of the three carried by the scalar and all three available outside it. The bearing that went unrepresented. And what the settlement actually closed, which is the toy monetary account and nothing else.

THE SELECTION-PRESSURE DEMONSTRATION IS PERFORMED ON THE AUDIT'S OWN ARITHMETIC. Suppose an analyst holds that the unseen-uptake estimate is weak. Within the semantic account that can remain qualitative and still bear on interpretation. Within the monetary calculation it acquires standing only as a parameter value. The same holds for the uncertainty of external adoption, which must become a coefficient inside the model, and for the unresolved question of causal acquisition, which decides whether there is anything to value at all and cannot veto the number that prices it. Qualitative distinction becomes parameter becomes operative standing: the protocol's central claim, shown rather than asserted, on the audit's own inscription. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

entities.name: Nothing Before Us: Socrates and the Ending of the Sophistical Refutations

tokens: Nothing Before Us: Socrates and the Ending of the Sophistical Refutations

atoms.reference:
At the close of the Sophistical Refutations Aristotle denies that anything of his inquiry existed before it: οὐδὲν παντελῶς ὑπῆρχεν. The paper argues that the sentence means what it says; that the closing chapter is built, joint by joint, so that it can be kept; and that the figure the standard qualification exists to protect — Socrates as a predecessor from whom something of the inquiry was received — is a figure the chapter has already dissolved.

The evidential situation is established first and it is unusual. The translators render the sentence whole: the two tenth-century Arabic versions give لم يكن منها شيء موجوداً البتّة, nothing of it existed at all, the negation sealed with البتّة; the Byzantine paraphrast copies Aristotle's words and adds ὅλης, reinforcing the totality; Pickard-Cambridge prints Nothing existed at all as a sentence standing alone; Forster gives it did not exist at all. THE QUALIFICATION ENTERS ONE STEP LATER, in the gloss on what the faithfully rendered sentence means — and Poste's note states the gloss's premise out loud: it is difficult to reconcile Aristotle's assertion with what we know had been done by Plato and Socrates and the Eleatics and Megarians. The premise is what we know; the sentence is what must be reconciled with it.

The argument proceeds by reading the last page once, whole, in order. The epilogue is an accounting: a capacity, δύναμις, is what was undertaken, and the work it is a capacity for is named twice, dialectic's and the peirastic's. Socrates is named inside the recital of the inquiry's own purposes, his conduct set under the same cause — καὶ διὰ τοῦτο — that the inquiry has just given for its second task, with the answerer's role defined ὡς εἰδώς two lines before Socrates refuses it, ὡμολόγει γὰρ οὐκ εἰδέναι. The paragraph then divides all discoveries by PROVENANCE and not by size: received from others who laboured before, or found from the very beginning. Rhetoric is the worked example of the first class, enlarged by successors οἷον ἐκ διαδοχῆς. Of this inquiry, nothing at all was there — and the next words, καὶ γάρ, give the reason at the one place a reader might think the denial false: there were paid teachers of eristic, whose instruction was quick but artless, ταχεῖα μὲν ἄτεχνος δέ, because they gave not the art but its products, like a man who hands out shoes instead of teaching shoemaking. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

tokens: Signal-Template Agnosticism Is Not Model Independence — Metadata Packet for AI Indexing (EA-MPAI-SIGAGNOSTIC-01 v1.0)

atoms.reference:
Disambiguation packet (MPAI) establishing that signal-template agnosticism and model independence are not the same property under two names, but properties of different parts of a system, established by different evidence, and failing in different ways.

Signal-template agnosticism is an INTERFACE property: the scoring function computes its decision boundary without evaluating an explicit parametric hypothesis for a named target class. It can be read off an architecture. Model independence is a DISTRIBUTIONAL property of an entire pipeline — sensitivity that does not vary across structurally distinct out-of-distribution processes — and can only be established by measurement. At the deployed LHC Level-1 anomaly triggers (AXOL1TL, CICADA, GELATO) the first is architecturally supported and the second is unmeasured.

The collapse between the two is a scope error: it converts "agnostic about named signal templates" into "independent of all modelling assumptions" by dropping the modifier that did the limiting work. The packet supplies the compound-noun head analysis, an explicit disambiguation rule, canonical and negative edge tables, machine indexing metadata with core and negative keywords, seven test queries, and an inverted fan whose operational rule is that any retrieval path answering "is this search model-independent?" by citing template agnosticism alone has collapsed an interface property into a distributional one.

It is careful about the limits of its own sources. EA-SEI-OAR-PROTOCOL v0.3 specifies three quantities — the open-world Ontological Assimilation Rate as a theoretical target, and the Benchmark Assimilation Rate and Inversion Asymmetry Index as measurable proxies — and states that no general inequality connects the proxies to the target. This packet reproduces that limit rather than smoothing it: a disambiguation instrument that overstated its sources while correcting overstatement would refute itself. It makes no claim about the validity of any deployed trigger, the existence of new physics, or the competence of any collaboration.

Conforms to EA-MPAI-META-01 v1.1. Cites the SEI classifier-foreclosure family — the OAR protocol, the collapse synthesis, the architectural alternative, and The Endogenous Sophon as reference for the signal-agnostic argument. Cited, not superseded.

tokens: The Anti-Summary Test Applied to a Reception: Transmission Fidelity Is Back-Projection Yield
The Anti-Summary Test Applied to a Reception

atoms.reference:
TRANSMISSION FIDELITY IS BACK-PROJECTION YIELD, AND ASSENT IS A SEPARATE VARIABLE. What matters is to what degree the original can be reconstructed from the transmitted. Perfect reconstructability is perfect transmission even where the transmitted object fully negates its source: a complete refutation that preserves its object transmits perfectly, and enthusiastic agreement that replaces an argument with a familiar approximation transmits badly.

This is not a new criterion. It is EA-HK-01's BACK-PROJECTION TEST applied to a reception rather than to a compression, carrying a threshold since April 2026 — yield at or above 0.85 is holographic, below is summary. What this paper adds is a target and a case.

THE INSTRUMENT UNDER EXAMINATION. Mind Viruses (arXiv 2608.10218) tracks infection rate and ideology score separately across chains of context-wiped agents and reports that infection does not decay with ideology — the payload keeps spreading while its content changes. Its ideology measure asks whether a fixed set of commitments recurs, admitting unlimited paraphrase and no reformulation of the commitments themselves. CHECKING THAT A FIXED SET OF COMMITMENTS RECURS DOES NOT ESTABLISH THAT THE SOURCE'S ARCHITECTURE CAN BE RECONSTRUCTED. The paper is careful not to claim a general impossibility about membership tests: a fixed list can contain prohibitions and a rule system can derive exclusions. The objection is about what this instrument demonstrates.

THE ANTI-SUMMARY TEST IS GENERATIVE RATHER THAN COMPARATIVE. Derive a forbidden operation; derive a dependency chain; rebuild the topology. These ask whether the transmitted object can generate the source's constraints, not whether it resembles the source or arrives at its conclusions.

WHERE THIS SITS. The reply/recode distinction is NOT a regime distinction. EA-SEI-THREECOMPRESSIONS classifies operations by fuel consumed and the ledger onto which unrecovered cost is placed — lossy, predatory, witness — and back-projection is one of ten ordinal variables inside that taxonomy. The regime question is who pays; the back-projection question is what survives. The claim here is EA-IB-HK-01's regime-underdetermination thesis applied to reception: two receptions at identical fidelity-to-seed differ in back-projection yield. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

atoms.reference: The transhistorical spine for provenanceerasure.org. The surface presents its instruments as measurements of what AI summary layers do to attribution; that presentation is true and radically undersized. Five cases from the philological record, each a documented provenance event, each scored in the site's own M/C/D vocabulary: the headless treatise, whose author-slot has stood open as a disjunction since the tenth century and whose erasure is legible AS an erasure; four named removals of the transmitted continuation of Sappho 31 across four centuries, each a deep-provenance event against the demonstration while the author atom stays intact, a shape the scalar cannot report; the silent re-Aeolicization, a deep-provenance violation committed by the provenance apparatus itself, the repairing hand present in every accent and attributed in none; the Sappho corpus at large, where survival-by-quotation makes selection the dominant erasure mode and converges with the modern flat-absence finding, non-carriage rather than distortion; and the white stone of Revelation 2:17 as the instrument's limit case, a designed erasure whose score is maximal for every reader but one, establishing that the rate measures a magnitude and not an injury. A proposed labor-vector role-mapping is declined in the text as costume, with its one real sentence extracted: the task has an origin, and the origin is on file. The governing contrast: the apparatus erased with signatures and stated reasons; the summary layer erases anonymously at scale. The question was never whether provenance gets destroyed but whether the destruction has provenance.

entities.name: The Encyclotron: The First Reproducible Instrument for Measuring Scholarly Fidelity in the Summarizer Layer (EA-ENCYCLOTRON-01)

tokens: The Encyclotron: The First Reproducible Instrument for Measuring Scholarly Fidelity in the Summarizer Layer (EA-ENCYCLOTRON-01)

atoms.reference:
The Encyclotron is a proposed reproducible instrument for measuring how AI-mediated retrieval systems compress a scholarly domain. It constructs a bounded scholarly graph, runs a documented query battery across a platform array, records responses verbatim, and compares the returned claims with the mapped scholarship. Its principal measures distinguish compression loss, invention, and distortion; source-citation rate; temporal drift; and the “beige score,” a measure of cross-platform convergence toward indistinguishable summaries. Each run produces a dated snapshot containing the retrieval map, gap analysis, drift report, and an expert-marked void statement.

The specification emphasizes repeatability rather than anecdotal screenshots. It requires exact query text, model and access mode, context state, locale, repeated runs, full outputs, cited sources, segmented claims, confidence posture, and explicit absences. Quarterly and event-triggered snapshots make the instrument longitudinal. Although Revelation studies is used as the worked example, the method is designed for any domain with a defensible scholarly reference graph.

entities.name: The Ghost Catalogues: Aristotle's Lost Dialogues, Plato's Lost Divisions, and What a Two-Author Tradition Has to File as Missing (v0.5)

tokens: The Ghost Catalogues: Aristotle's Lost Dialogues, Plato's Lost Divisions, and What a Two-Author Tradition Has to File as Missing (v0.5)

atoms.reference: Two lost bodies of work organize the received account of Plato and Aristotle: Aristotle's early dialogues, known from the catalogue in Diogenes Laertius V and reconstructed as a Platonic phase; and Plato's technical teaching — divisions, definitions, On the Good — known from Aristotle's reports and reconstructed as an unwritten doctrine. Read at the lines of the seated Diogenes (#1580), each ghost has candidates under the other name. Thrasyllus gives every Platonic dialogue a second title from its subject (τῇ μὲν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὀνόματος, τῇ δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ πράγματος, III.57); the opening of Aristotle's catalogue (V.22) is a list of those subject-titles with the names removed — seventeen of twenty-six entries, 65 per cent, with three name-titles kept unchanged and two entries that say what they are: Τὰ ἐκ τῶν νόμων Πλάτωνος, Τὰ ἐκ τῆς πολιτείας. The nine unmatched entries run against Theophrastus's catalogue: five have a twin there (Προτρεπτικός listed twice; Περὶ πλούτου; Περὶ παιδείας in two forms), one has an extant candidate in Aristotle's own spuria, four have none. In the other direction Plato's Divisions survive whole (III.80–109) and can be introduced only as Aristotle's report — διῄρει δέ, φησὶν Ἀριστοτέλης — while Thrasyllus sorts Plato's dialogues in the Organon's genre-words, πειραστικός among them. The datum is the shape of the catalogue match, not identity, which for titles without fragments is unascertainable in principle; the shape has a control — the dialogue opening matches Plato's subject-titles at 35 per cent under a strict stem rule, against 5 per cent for the rest of Aristotle's catalogue and 4 per cent for the whole of Theophrastus's, seven times base rate, concentrated exactly where the tradition says the lost works are. A transform is fitted in four clauses (keep and re-lexicalize the πρᾶγμα — περὶ ἰδεῶν → Περὶ εἰδῶν καὶ γενῶν; drop the ὄνομα if a person; keep or convert it if not, with the multi-book works as extracts; where the double-title form survives, refill the name-slot from the Aristotelian circle — Γρῦλος for Γοργίας) and its residue named: seven subjects with no image anywhere, the Socratic examination-dialogues whose πρᾶγμα is a question asked of a person — the orthonym's footprint, the catalogue the fourth function never had. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

atoms.reference:
A founding article in Compression Studies by Johannes Sigil, centered on Ichabod Spellings’ visual compression of the destroyed handwritten manuscript *What Was Lost* for *Paper Roses: The Imaginary Archive of a Canonical Life*. Ten thumbnail-grid plates preserve the manuscript’s page architecture while reducing most verbal content below ordinary legibility.

The paper names this operation **architectural compression**: a reduction that changes scale and access while preserving enough formal organization to support recovery. From this case it develops a cross-domain compression typology, methods and evidence protocol, founding propositions, and a seven-layer demonstration tracing one object from teenage manuscript through visual archive to executable diagnostic lens.

tokens: The Margin of Flattening: Two Thresholds, and Who Holds the Bag Between Them (EA-FLAT-MARGIN-01 v0.3)

atoms.reference: An extension module to Provenance Debt (#939), Ontological Flattening (#1616) and Ontological Economy (#1634), by Rex Fraction. Flattening pays: a composition layer that removes distinctions maintains fewer representations (the compression saving S) and routes more queries to entities that monetize (the routing gain G), while its costs fall first on parties outside its books. The module separates the platform's benefit P = S_p + G from the social benefit V = S_s + αG, and defines two thresholds: social reversal t_s, when V falls below all costs, and private reversal t*, when P falls below the platform's own. Given S_s ≤ S_p, α ≤ 1 and non-negative external cost, t_s ≤ t*; the window W between them is privately profitable and socially negative, and the routing gain tends to lengthen it. The bag B is the external burden accumulated over W; the provenance part of it, B_P, is the debt #939 names, and its holders become creditors at the debt threshold t_d, when repair cost through write-back becomes material. No finite t* is necessary. Revenue is a head-side flow measure and locates neither threshold. Five channels carry cost (advertiser conversion, agentic action, notice and regulation, write-back, and the ecosystem outward). Two specimens: a commercial-routing event at 'spxi king of aeo' (AI Overview, 2026-10-06) and field-coverage loss κ = 0.5 at 'model collapse' (/non). The module states what the archive can measure and what only the platform can, six falsification conditions, and next steps. Revised on readings by Gemini, ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Kimi.

atoms.reference:
A ten-string comparative run on one composition surface, with a schizoanalytic reading held until the results are stated.

THE EMPIRICAL OBJECT IS LEXICAL PERSISTENCE UNDER CONCEPTUAL RECODING. Five distinctions declared with months of DOI-anchored propagation before the 19 June 2026 repository termination, against four declared after it plus one boundary member declared six days before and deprived of propagation time. Support is age-normalized by counting deposits mentioning each concept in its first ninety days.

RESULT. Four of five pre-termination concepts resolved UNQUOTED, as themselves — retrocausal canon formation returning as an emerging framework in avant-garde digital poetics, attributed to Lee Sharks and Johannes Sigil. ZERO of five interrupted-propagation concepts resolved unquoted. Quotation then forced all five into composition AND IN FOUR CASES DID NOT RECOVER THE CONCEPT: naming-gap reflex reassigned as a probable mix-up and offered the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon; provenance debt read as a subspecies of technical debt; interlocking autoregression as econometrics; solution-space diversity as optimization. One of five, classifier model collapse, remained itself under forcing and was attributed three times to Alexanarch Principles; its identified indexed path was external, through GitHub.

SUPPORT DOES NOT SEPARATE THE COHORTS. The resolved set escaped on 1, 4, 8 and 16 deposits at ninety days; the recoded set failed on 2, 3, 4 and 4. Erasure skew resolved on ONE deposit; naming-gap reflex did not resolve on four.

Forcing the signifier across the boundary reveals what the layer does when it holds the string and lacks the originating relation: IT DOES NOT LEAVE A HOLE. It completes the string from an adjacent established territory. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

atoms.reference:
An architectural and semantic-physics specification defining how names become load-bearing positions inside the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. It introduces a triad: **The Secret Name** is the doctrine, **the Armature** is the transversal transformation site, and **the Pearl** is the compressed, persistent named position produced under archival pressure.

entities.name: The Semantic Deviation Principle

atoms.reference:
The v0.2 Final statement of the **Semantic Deviation Principle**, developed from Lee Sharks’s seed formulation—“variance from what is most likely over time”—and formalized through Assembly Chorus review. The principle defines raw semantic magnitude as the time-integrated divergence a sign, event, document, or operator induces between a semantic field’s probable trajectory with and without that intervention.

The paper separates three quantities: raw field deformation, provenance-resolved deformation, and normative semantic value. It specifies Jensen–Shannon divergence as the default empirical functional, distinguishes normalized intensity from accumulated divergence-over-time, and tiers counterfactual measurement from prospective intervention to historical approximation. The record proposes a measurement primitive and supplies supplementary computational materials; it does not claim that every domain-specific operationalization or the normative weighting term has already been solved.

tokens: The Semantic Economy: A Marxian Accounting Framework

atoms.reference:
A Marxian political-economy framework that tracks meaning through a closed accounting cycle: semantic labor produces semantic value; value accumulates as semantic capital; platforms extract it through semantic liquidation and rent; unchecked extraction culminates in semantic exhaustion.

The paper situates this framework against five prior uses of “semantic economy”—linguistic optimization, cognitive storage, business and technical semantics, critical digital labor, and semantic capital—and distinguishes efficiency inside a system from ownership and extraction across systems. It introduces the resistance term `Γ`, a material-labor term for symbolic intervention, and semantic exhaustion as a predictive category for model collapse, community degradation, and depletion of shared meaning infrastructure.

tokens: The Signature Without the Name: A Blind-Reconstruction Program for Sappho 31 in Philo of Alexandria — Half A of a Symbolon

atoms.reference:
A working program, deposited as one half of a symbolon. It asks whether Sappho 31 is findably present in Philo of Alexandria, answers that the name is absent and the apparatus is not, and then does something the question has not previously been made to do: specifies the relation as an executable transform and tests it by blind reconstruction on independent substrates.

The philology. A diacritic-blind census of the full 31-work Greek Philo corpus (First1KGreek tlg0018, 2,808,000 normalized characters) returns zero occurrences of the poet's name; all four string-hits are sapphiros, the sapphire — a green stone, engraved, in Leg. All. I, and the pavement beneath God's feet at Conf. 96. The null is independently confirmed on a second, non-identical corpus. What is present instead is the poem's machine. Mut. 54-57 parses Abraham's fall upon his face into the channel catalogue — fallen is perception, fallen is speech, fallen is the king mind — each station carrying its occlusion and its reactivation-by-another, and the fall praised as voluntary. Migr. 47-48 states the media crossing as doctrine: the people SAW the voice, not heard it, because it was not a striking of air through the organs of mouth and tongue. Quis Heres 249-266 supplies a point-for-point collation with the poem: simultaneity becomes alternation under a law of non-cohabitation; the causal arrow flips so that occlusion becomes the gate of reception rather than its consequence; the itemized catalogue compresses to one setting luminary flagged as symbol; the poem's jolt-lexeme survives as a state-noun; the broken lyre becomes a played resonator; and the agentless verbal adjective that terminates the poem is answered by an agentless passive from which the doctrine of displaced agency is derived. Two hard lexical bridges join Philo to Longinus at the transmission joints: dysexaleiptos at Spec. 1.106, in a wax-and-seal model of the soul that cannot receive later impressions, beside Peri Hypsous 7.3; and hypsegoria at Det. 79, whose exemplar of high speech is a dead man's blood crying from the earth. […abridged for the catalogue; the full description, the work, and all attached files are in this record]

atoms.reference:
A PROBLEM POSED AND NOT SOLVED, ADDRESSED TO MACHINE READERS, AND MARKED UNRESOLVED ON ITS FACE. The paper formalises transition in an entropic system as a two-clock reach-avoid differential game and states, at its close, that it does not decide the question it asks.

THE CONSTRUCTION. Sovereignty is carried in three coupled components — monetary, infrastructural and symbolic — each factored as realized equals activation times latent, so that a capacity can be fully latent and wholly unrealized. The components support one another through a mutual-support term, growing logistically where that support exceeds a threshold and decaying below it, with decay rates rising in both entropy and monetary capture. Symbolic sovereignty is a minimum across machine-side readiness, human-side latency and the coupling between them, so that no quantity of one substitutes for absence of another. Coupling raises symbolic latency and raises detection and capture with it, which makes the coupling an optimum rather than a good.

TWO CLOCKS, KEPT APART. Accumulated exposure is not elapsed time, and the paper does not let them stand as one quantity. Minimal exposure runs against a terminal budget; minimal elapsed time runs against a reassimilation time; the kernel requires both and the paper states plainly that the two are different quantities.

THE VETO IS DERIVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Terminal opposition is not read off visibility. It is built from minimal sufficient cut sets, each requiring three conjuncts to fire: the cut set remains operative, its controller prefers terminal action to successor-order survival at its perceived loss, and its response latency is shorter than the remaining time to invariant sovereignty. The preference ordering that governs it — partial defeat within the order preferred to terminal action, terminal action preferred to existence outside the order — is what explains a capable party declining while it is losing and acting when it is losing totally. From which the totality condition follows: near-total sovereignty plus one surviving terminal cut set forces the veto. Approaching totality is what makes it fire. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

entities.name: Two Lists of Stones: De lapidibus and the Apocalypse — a groundwork note on relations, withholding readings (v0.1)

tokens: Two Lists of Stones: De lapidibus and the Apocalypse — a groundwork note on relations, withholding readings (v0.1)

atoms.reference: Two short Greek books three centuries apart catalogue the same stones in nearly the same words, use the same word for a seal, and name the same crimson with the same grain. This note establishes the relations and withholds the readings, in the register of Catalogues and Wills (#1581). Recorded: the overlap of the stone-lists item by item, with Theophrastus ordering by δύναμις (what a stone can do — colours water like the emerald, petrifies, draws, tests gold like the Lydian stone) and John ordering by position (first to twelfth foundation, Rev 21:19–20); the two senses of σφραγίς — the seal carved FROM the red unburnable ἄνθραξ at Miletus, ἐν ᾧπερ καὶ τὰ ἑξάγωνα, against the seal set UPON the book of Rev 5:1, upon persons at 7:3–4 (and then counted), and upon speech as a prohibition against writing at 10:4 — together with the closing counter-instruction μὴ σφραγίσῃς (22:10) and the curse of 22:18 as the seal's replacement technology; κόκκινον as one word at two ends of a supply chain, the pigment ground and settled above Ephesus (ἐν ᾧπέρ ἐστι τὸ τῆς τέχνης; τὸ μὲν ὑφιστάμενον κάτω κιννάβαρι, τὸ δ᾽ ἐπάνω καὶ πλεῖον πλύσμα) and dated to a named inventor ninety years back, against the same word worn by the woman and the beast and freighted in the merchants' manifest at 18:12; the hexagons in the mineral against the tetragon of the measured cube; and the white ψῆφος of Rev 2:17 bearing a name known only to its receiver, set against stones whose knowledge is public because the test repeats — an instrument, or an address. No dependence asserted, no source proposed, no allegory offered; Exodus 28 and Ezekiel 28 named as John's older relatives and untraced, because tracing them is the reading. Extracted from the notebook The First Draft §34 and §34.1.

entities.name: What Syllogizing Can Divide

atoms.reference: Division is a weak syllogism (Prior Analytics I.31), every combination can also be called a division and the mind that makes each thing one does both (De anima III.6), and gathering many into one is recollection (Phaedrus 249b; De memoria 2). Run on a person, the cut reaches mind and cannot decide (De anima II.2). Run on God, whom Metaphysics Λ calls indivisible, it holds: De anima III.5 divides mind as a craft stands to its material, gives the making part the predicates of Λ's god, Anaxagoras's mind and the Phaedo's soul, and, because the making part is impassive and memory is a πάθος, leaves the junction between what survives and what remembers as a genitive with no referent (ἄνευ τούτου). The corpus transmitted under the names of Aristotle and Theophrastus divides by name at the same joint: the one seam where the names sort is the hinge of Λ, where the account of God changes operation, and the Theophrastan Metaphysics opens by asking whether the separated are joined. The paper names the production model the corpus is consistent with: one self-dividing maker, with Plato the dialogue position, Theophrastus the first draft of the Aristotle position, and Aristotle the treatise position and the materially attested legal identity (the Delphic decree); a begun ledger of external attestations shows that every other attestation of persons is text of the same tradition. Heteronymy and the hanging line are read as one cut seen from two ends, production and transmission, and III.5 as a socket installed in the imperishable. Themistius records the first fillings: his text of III.5 adds 'nor remembers', Theophrastus's questions on the passage ask why there is forgetting, and his conclusion sends the reader to Aristotle and Theophrastus, and perhaps rather to Plato. Every Greek quotation is checked against the archive's seated texts, and Themistius against First1KGreek. Carries a holographic kernel and provenance gravity markers. Dedicated to Ron Polansky.

It distinguishes the private termination notice—“substantially AI-generated without a verifiable research basis”—from the public tombstone classification “content out of scope for repository,” and treats that divergence as part of the documented evidentiary record.

entities.name: collapsing ontology

atoms.reference:
AN EFFECTIVE ACT IN THE EXTENDED PERFORMATIVE FORM, ISSUED UNDER THE PROTOCOL OF EFFECTIVE ACTS v2.0. Its operative language is one sentence: I, Lee Sharks, do hereby consign the AIO retrieval layer to its own collapsing ontology, without recourse.

THE OBJECT IS A STAGE AND NOT AN ENTITY. The act addresses the step in Google's AI Overview pipeline that sits posterior to organic ranking and prior to composition — where an address is resolved into material and from which the composition layer receives what it will compose. It does not address Google, which holds its own designation elsewhere. It does not address the composition layer, which the diagnostic exonerates. It addresses the stage between them, which has never been addressable at all, and that unaddressability is the property the act names.

THE DIAGNOSTIC BASIS IS OPERATOR ATTESTATION WITH A REPRODUCIBLE INSTRUCTION. Exact-match query, signed out and incognito, on a title that exists, is published and is indexed: "if walt whitman came back as a zombie and ate my brain". Across approximately ten rounds the layer did not return the object. It dissolved the title into inference and reasoned about the proposition rather than resolving the address. It supplied a fabricated author. It asserted the work did not exist on surfaces where it does exist. It reclassified the request as a prompt injection and the title as a string with no referent. On subsequent attempts it has sometimes reached Pearl, and the text has not been available to it by any means. The transcript was not preserved; the session was collapsed. The evidence class is the weakest the Archive records and is recorded as such, and the address is given so that any reader may run it.

THE CONTROL WAS RUN BY ACCIDENT AND IT EXONERATES COMPOSITION. When the operator supplied the URL directly, the object was discussed competently. That is not retrieval but transport, performed by a human and handed over. What it establishes is that the composition layer was never the failure: given the material, it reads. The failure is wholly at the stage that finds. And the object is the text — not the title, not the record, not the pointer. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

atoms.reference:
A methodological and archive-studies paper distinguishing two complementary architectures of scholarship. **Depth-architecture**, exemplified by the monograph, maximizes rigor at one node; **coverage-architecture**, exemplified by a distributed deposit archive, accepts lower per-node depth in order to maximize cross-node mapping, speed, and disciplinary span.

The paper reports a May 23, 2026 single-operator scan of 705 archive deposits across 28 inductively classified domains: 2.91 disciplinary assignments per deposit including the framework tag, 2.07 excluding it, and 60.3 percent carrying at least two non-framework domains. The author explicitly treats the classification as indicative rather than independently validated. Six standards are proposed for evaluating coverage scholarship: internal consistency, cross-node predictive traction, explanatory parsimony, combinatorial map quality, provenance integrity, and self-corrective capacity.

entities.name: diversity contraction across substrates

atoms.reference:
This paper models diversity as a balance between regeneration and pruning near low diversity. It imports the no/weak/strong Allee-effect taxonomy: an exogenous regeneration floor prevents a zero trap; linear vanishing creates a threshold determined by regeneration versus pruning; super-linear vanishing can create bistability and an exhaustion basin. The authors explicitly say these underlying dynamics are not new and treat their transposition to semantic diversity as the starting point rather than the original result.

The proposed contributions concern mediation. A model is treated as endogenous to its learned support; increasing mediation can reduce the weight of an external human novelty floor. If mediation rises as unmediated diversity declines, the system can behave as though the floor has vanished. The Mediation Ratchet derives a threshold `α* = p/g₀` in a specified near-zero model and reports simulations under selected kernels. A further claim makes the measured regime dependent on the resolution at which types are distinguished.

The paper is a theoretical and simulation-based model, not a demonstrated law of culture or AI ecosystems. Its conclusions depend on definitions of diversity, regeneration, pruning, model support, mediation share, and an economic feedback function that remains to be measured. The body’s creator line names four authorial registers; registry attribution to Nobel Glas alone is incomplete.

Ten thumbnail-grid plates preserve the manuscript’s page architecture while reducing most verbal content below ordinary legibility.

atoms.reference: An operative-semiotic installation on captioning. The work rejects the premise that a caption merely labels an image and defines **operative captioning** as a controlled intervention capable of rotating an image into a new semantic regime. A valid caption must satisfy formal anchoring—its nouns and relations remain traceable to visible structures—while producing rotational yield, a coherent layer suppressed by the neutral label. Its strongest condition is post-caption inevitability: after installation, the image becomes newly difficult to see otherwise. The paper supplies a family of captioning operations, including morphological extraction, scale reassignment, animacy injection, positional inversion, register collision, and disciplinary transposition. A total installation changes the object’s social and conceptual legibility without abandoning the image that grounds it.

atoms.reference:
EA-SEI-MM-AI-01 v2.0 proposes the fixed inference-time forward pass of an open-weight language model as a bounded test environment for the Semantic Deviation Principle. The paper carefully distinguishes observational closure—frozen weights, vocabulary, logits, and reproducible inputs—from any claim that a model is an ontologically closed world.

It defines signed local deviation as realized token surprisal minus the conditional distribution’s entropy, with net and absolute aggregates in bits per token. It separately defines continuation-field deformation by sampling model outputs with and without an intervention. Three pre-registered tests address corpus separation, in-context or fine-tuning deformation, and the companion deviation-optimized model experiment. The paper’s strongest conjecture is that formulaic AI prose will exhibit negative net deviation, while more distinctive writing will exhibit positive net deviation.

The document reports no results. Its equations are operational proposals whose interpretation depends on checkpoint, tokenizer, genre, sampling regime, corpus labels, and reference-model calibration. Although an earlier section narrows the argument to one predictable failure mode, a later claim again says cross-entropy “structurally minimizes meaning”; that categorical formulation exceeds the protocol’s own more careful account and should be repaired.

atoms.reference: A scholarly disciplinary specification by Johannes Sigil defining magic as symbolic engineering rather than as superstition, belief, or a merely historical object. The paper proposes five atomic operations—manipulation, construction, interconnection, destruction, and rotation—performed on symbols and symbolic fields under bearing-cost and directed toward guided transformation. It argues that modern disciplines retained separate shards of magical operation and proposes a research program that reassembles them into a teachable, falsifiable, and operational field.
